newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan finance chief says no bond issue for now.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan finance chief says no bond issue for now.

text.p: Pakistan should wait a few months before trying to float a bond issue, its outgoing finance chief Shahid Javed Burki said on Thursday.
"I think we should wait for another couple of months," the finance and economic affairs adviser to caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid told Reuters in an interview.
"If I had anything to do with economic management in the next few months, I would say that Pakistan should seriously explore the possibility of a bond issue some time in March or April," he added.
Burki will return to his job as a World Bank vice-president once the caretaker government hands over to its elected successor after Monday's national and provincial polls.

He explored the possibility of a Samurai bond issue during the government's 90-day term, but prospects dimmed when Moody's Investors Service Inc downgraded Pakistan's sovereign foreign-currency debt to B2 from B1 on November 8.
The downgrade, which Burki called a "wrong decision", had made it "exceedingly difficult to borrow in the market".
He said Moody's had taken its decision before President Farooq Leghari sacked Benazir Bhutto's government on November 5.
"Since then what we have accomplished is absolutely marvellous, if I may say so myself," Burki said.

"My message to the international community is that Pakistan is poised to move forward in a very responsible way in restructuring its economy and producing the right kind of incentives for the private sector to come in.
"So it's a business-friendly place with a lot of potential. I think foreign investors should take note of it," he added.
